analysis.summary: Create a five-page static website hosted on a private S3 bucket, delivered via CloudFront with a custom domain and HTTPS enabled using ACM certificates. Implement HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection.
requirements: Host a five-page static website on S3.
Use a private S3 bucket as the origin for CloudFront.
Set up CloudFront distribution to deliver the website content.
Configure a custom domain for the website using Route 53.
Obtain and attach a valid HTTPS certificate from ACM to CloudFront.
Implement HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection for all incoming requests.
service_dependencies: CloudFront for content delivery and HTTPS termination.
Route 53 for DNS management and custom domain configuration.
ACM for provisioning and managing SSL/TLS certificates.
risks: Ensuring the S3 bucket is private while allowing CloudFront access requires correct bucket policy configuration.
Properly configuring HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects in CloudFront may require additional behaviors or Lambda@Edge (not listed as allowed service).
Certificate validation for ACM may require DNS validation via Route 53.
questions: What is the custom domain name to be used?
Are the five pages already created and ready to upload?
Should the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect be handled solely by CloudFront behaviors or is another mechanism preferred?
Is DNS hosted in Route 53 or elsewhere?
Are there any specific caching or performance requirements for CloudFront?
